dedupe_keys.name: european nuclear stress tests complementary safety assessments of french installations and the eu peer review asn 2011 to 2012

description: This case study documents the European nuclear stress tests that followed the Fukushima accident of 11 March 2011, through the page of the French Nuclear Safety Authority, ASN, now ASNR. ASN asked operators on 5 May 2011 to carry out complementary safety assessments of their installations, based on specifications approved by ENSREG, the European nuclear regulators group, covering all installations including research and fuel processing sites. Seventy-nine installations were high priority, among them 58 EDF reactors, and their operators reported on 15 September 2011; other installations were to report by 15 September 2012, and a French final report went to the European Commission by the end of 2011. The page also notes the EU final report adopted on 26 April 2012 and ASN's criticism of the Commission's conclusions in October 2012. Access: the page is free and public; no licence is stated. Coverage is France within the EU exercise. Caveats: this is the French regulator's account, the European peer review reports on the ENSREG site were not readable in this session, and the outcomes for other countries are not covered. It suits risk and vulnerability assessment and policy evaluation studies of nuclear plant safety after external hazards, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

outcomes: The French complementary safety assessments covered 79 high-priority installations, including 58 EDF reactors, whose operators reported on 15 September 2011, with a final French report due to the European Commission by 31 December 2011; the EU-level stress test final report was adopted on 26 April 2012, and ASN publicly regretted the Commission's later conclusions of 4 October 2012 for ignoring important recommendations.
